about: The engine's own setup guides and capability sets (platform/runtime/venture/build/guides.ts guideOf, connector-truth.ts connectorCapabilities) for the fake's connectors, copied by W4 4J21.

steps: 1. Sign in to Lovable in your browser.
2. In Chausar, open the brief and choose Lovable.
3. Read the brief in Lovable and press send there yourself.
guide.skipped: Turn on GitHub sync in Lovable, so Chausar can follow the code.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: There is nothing to connect, so there is no access to check: you sign in to Lovable yourself.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing by itself. Chausar fills in or copies the brief; you press send in Lovable.
guide.agentLimits: Agents can't open Lovable or send anything to it.

steps: 1. On GitHub, make a fine-grained personal access token.
2. Under Repository access, choose Only select repositories and pick the one repo your builder uses.
3. Under Repository permissions, set Contents and Metadata to Read-only, and Actions and Deployments to Read-only for the build checks. Leave every other permission at No access.
4. Set an end date, then paste the token and the repo address in Chausar.
guide.skipped: Set an end date on the token, so a lost token stops working on its own.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: Chausar does not read GitHub when you link the repo. It reads it when you press Check GitHub, and Check connections reads the repo page once.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing, so nothing here can change your repo. Chausar reads it and never pushes.
guide.agentLimits: Agents can't read or change the repo. Only the build page reads it.

steps: 1. Nothing to connect.
2. Chausar drafts the message or the invoice email.
3. Open it in your own mail app and press send yourself.
guide.skipped: Read the draft before you send it: Chausar never sends it for you.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.sends: Sends: nothing. You send each message yourself, from your own mailbox.
guide.agentLimits: Agents can only propose an email. It waits for your approval, and you send it yourself.

steps: 1. Turn on 2-Step Verification for your Google account.
2. Under Security, then App passwords, make an app password for Chausar. A Workspace admin can block app passwords; then this does not work for that account.
3. Use the desktop app: under Connections, type imap.gmail.com, port 993, your address and that password.
4. Chausar keeps it only while the app is open, so type it again after Chausar restarts.
guide.skipped: Turn on 2-Step Verification first: without it Google offers no app passwords.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: Chausar signs in and opens your inbox read only before it keeps anything, so a wrong password is refused at once. Check connections does the same again.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing, so nothing here can change your Gmail mail. Chausar reads read only and never marks a message read.
guide.agentLimits: Agents can't read your mailbox. Only replies from people in your network and pipeline reach Today, screened first.

steps: 1. In Zoho Mail, open Settings, then Mail Accounts, and check that IMAP Access is on.
2. In your Zoho account, open Security, then App Passwords, and make an app-specific password for Chausar.
3. Use the desktop app: under Connections, type the server (imap.zoho.com, or imap.zoho.in for an account in India), port 993, your address and that password.
4. Chausar keeps it only while the app is open, so type it again after Chausar restarts.
guide.skipped: Make an app-specific password: with two-factor sign-in on, your Zoho password itself does not work over IMAP.

2. If Chausar says Playwright with Chromium is missing, install it first.
3. Press Sign in and sign in to LinkedIn yourself, in the Chausar browser window. Chausar never sees your password.
4. Run the posting steps check, then approve each post on Today.
guide.skipped: Run the posting steps check before the first post, so Chausar knows the page still works the way it expects.

guide.agentLimits: Agents can only propose a post. Each one waits for your approval, and none goes out on its own.

steps: 1. Open the employer’s public Greenhouse jobs page and copy its board name. No API key is needed.
2. In the recruiting role, choose this provider and board, then set the exact job filters.
3. Read and approve the board and filters before installation. Read it again when you want fresh matches.
guide.skipped: Use the employer’s public board name, not an applicant profile or private hiring dashboard.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: Installation reads the public board. The first read seeds current jobs without alerts; later reads compare new matching jobs.
guide.sends: Sends: a public jobs read only. No applications, candidate profiles or messages are sent.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot apply, contact candidates or change the approved board filters themselves.

steps: 1. In the client WordPress profile, create a separate credential under Application Passwords for a user allowed to create drafts.
2. In the SEO desk, enter the HTTPS site address, username and application password for this session.
3. Review the current client-approved article, approve saving its exact draft, then publish it yourself in WordPress.
guide.skipped: Use a dedicated user with only the needed draft permissions. An application password inherits that user’s access; it is not a draft-only permission.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: Saving settings does not test WordPress credentials. The approved draft request checks the response; the later public-page check verifies the approved article.
guide.sends: Sends: only the exact client and owner approved article as a draft. The owner publishes it.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot publish, email or retry an unknown result. Check WordPress yourself if the save is uncertain.

steps: 1. Ask the client developer for the existing Worker, namespace, account ID and exact override key.
2. Create an API token with Workers KV Storage Write access for only the chosen account, then enter its token, namespace ID and site in the SEO desk.
3. Review the existing value and client-approved replacement, then approve the exact change. Undo asks separately.
guide.skipped: The client must already have a Worker using this namespace. Chausar does not install one or create the namespace.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: Saving settings checks their shape, not live access. Staging reads the existing key; applying checks the saved value. Changes can take time to appear elsewhere.
guide.sends: Sends: only an exact approved existing-key replacement or separately approved undo.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot provision Workers, change other keys or retry an unknown write. Inspect uncertain results manually.

steps: 1. In the lead desk, choose a city area and the kind of business you want to research.
2. Review the bounded area and run the one-off public map search. No key is needed.
3. Check the returned sources and keep OpenStreetMap attribution with any reused data.
guide.skipped: OpenStreetMap coverage can be incomplete. Keep attribution and the ODbL licence on derived databases.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: There is no sign-in check. The requested bounded Overpass query either returns public map records or a clear refusal.
guide.sends: Sends: only the chosen public map query. It does not contact businesses or change OpenStreetMap.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot turn missing map details into verified emails or run unrestricted scraping.

steps: 1. Read https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ before using the public city lookup.
2. Enter a city name deliberately in the lead desk. Never send personal addresses or confidential text.
3. Check the returned city area. If lookup is unavailable, choose the city box manually.
guide.skipped: Use city lookups only. No autocomplete, repeated bulk geocoding, systematic area searches or resale of geocoding results.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: No key is checked. Deliberate lookups are cached and serialised with at most one request per second.
guide.sends: Sends: the requested city name to the public Nominatim service, not a customer address.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot use this as a general address service. Respect the linked policy and keep map attribution.

steps: 1. Choose the business’s own public website for a lead in the lead desk.
2. Request the limited contact-page read only where the site terms permit it.
3. Review each found contact and its source before keeping or using it.
guide.skipped: Chausar obeys robots and reads the homepage plus at most three same-host contact pages. A refusal is not bypassed.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: There is no account check. Public page reads use the network and source-policy guards; missing details remain missing.
guide.sends: Sends: public page requests only. No forms, emails or messages are submitted.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot guess email addresses, enter private accounts or evade site restrictions.

steps: 1. Use your own Happenstance account and API key from its developer settings.
2. In the lead desk, write the exact search and read the dated credit quote.
3. Enter your key for this search and approve the displayed query and credit cost together.
guide.skipped: The query can use your network. Check the exact text and current credit quote before approving; a key alone is not permission to spend.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: There is no separate key test. The exact approved search checks the provider response and records whether it was confirmed.
guide.sends: Sends: only the exact owner-approved paid search. Open the returned Happenstance result yourself.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot send outreach or retry an unknown search. Check your Happenstance account after an uncertain result.

steps: 1. Open the bookkeeping desk and choose the client organisation and finance cycle.
2. Create an owner self-client access token in the matching Zoho account region, with only the read and write access needed for your chosen accounting operation.
3. Save the token for this open session. Setup needs no invented customer or item IDs; invoice and settlement work needs explicit mappings.
4. Read the exact proposal and approve it. Master creation, initial opening balances and invoice issue each ask separately.
guide.skipped: Choose the correct client organisation and region. Reconnect after locking or reopening the app; a saved token is not an approval.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: This connector is fixture-tested. Preparation reads current provider identities and amounts; each approved write requires exact readback. Live account qualification is not claimed.
guide.sends: Sends: only an exact owner-approved supported invoice or credit-note draft, issue action, received settlement payment, missing master or initial organisation opening balance. No email, bank transfer, overwrite or silent retry.
guide.agentLimits: Agents can prepare source work but cannot send directly to Zoho. Unsupported tax, currency, inventory and setup profiles stay on the manual bookkeeper path.

steps: 1. Open the client article order and record your permission to use the episode.
2. Add the episode transcript as SRT, VTT or TXT, then choose it in the article desk.
3. Review the source and outline before drafting. Reuse a source only for the same client.
guide.skipped: Check that the file contains the episode words you may reuse, not unrelated private material.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar reads the selected file and binds drafts to its current source. There is no remote transcript account to check.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing for file import. Any later model request has its own preview and approval.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot borrow another client’s transcript or treat unsupported statements as source evidence.

steps: 1. Use the desktop app with ffmpeg and whisper.cpp already installed by you.
2. Record episode rights, select the local audio or video in the article desk and approve the source import.
3. Read the resulting transcript before drafting. If local tools are unavailable, add a transcript file instead.
guide.skipped: Local media is limited to 50 MB. For larger episodes, supply a transcript; Chausar does not install tools for you.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: The approved import copies the local source and checks the installed tools when transcription runs. Hosted web cannot run them.
guide.sends: Sends: no recording to a remote transcription service. Processing uses the installed tools on this computer.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot install software or claim a transcript exists when local processing fails.

steps: 1. Finish source review, the owner-approved outline and the article draft.
2. Complete the required client-use review and approve the exact final article and companion text.
3. Copy the approved handoff into the client publishing account and publish it yourself.
guide.skipped: A changed article needs fresh approval. No publishing password belongs in this handoff.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar checks the saved source and exact approval before preparing the handoff. It does not check a publishing account or prove publication.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing to a publisher. Copy and publish the approved article yourself.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot publish or mark a manual handoff as a confirmed live article.

steps: 1. Prepare the issue from approved sources in the newsletter desk. No sending-service key is needed.
2. Before importing a recipient list or exporting, obtain the named lawyer’s consent confirmation. Draft preparation remains available meanwhile.
3. Approve the exact issue and recipients, export HTML, plain text and recipient CSV, then send through your existing tool yourself.
guide.skipped: Consent review is not yet confirmed. Keep list use and export blocked until that review is genuinely recorded.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar checks current consent, suppression and exact approval before export. It does not connect to or test your sending account.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing. You import the approved files and send with your own newsletter tool.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot send email, bypass opt-outs or claim a successful delivery from an export.

steps: 1. Attach client evidence separately from the RFP in the tender order.
2. Choose pasted questions or an RFP file. For a workbook, map the sheet, question column, answer column and row range.
3. Review every extracted question and its type before drafting. Write commercial answers yourself.
guide.skipped: The RFP is a request, not evidence that the client meets it. Do not use a copied RFP as client evidence.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar binds questions and answers to current source bytes. Changed sources require import and approval again.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing for local reading. A later AI request shows its exact source payload and asks separately.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot borrow documents from another client, invent certifications or write commercial answers.

steps: 1. Resolve source gaps and approve every answer by type.
2. Review the exact export pack, including the issuer workbook mapping and source amount receipts, then approve export.
3. Check the current issuer instructions and submit through your own portal or mail account.
guide.skipped: A downloaded pack does not prove submission or acceptance. Check the issuer deadline and current terms yourself.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar rechecks source bytes, exact answers and approvals before export. It does not test a portal account.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing to the issuer. You submit the approved files yourself.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot log in to a tender portal, submit a bid or claim the issuer accepted it.

steps: 1. Use your own Google Cloud project with billing and Text-to-Speech enabled. Restrict its API key to that API.
2. Open the narration desk, choose the client order and save the project key. Saving does not make a test call.
3. Read the current text, licensed stock voice and exact computed cost. Approve that one request, then verify and listen to the actual audio.
guide.skipped: Client production waits for a named lawyer to confirm narration rights. Private manuscripts and cloning do not use this cloud route.

charges.line: Chausar has not checked its prices. Read its own pricing page before you sign up.

guide.checks: Saving a key does not contact Google or prove access. An approved call checks the actual response; an uncertain outcome is never retried automatically.
guide.sends: Sends: only the exact approved text and stock voice to Google, paid on your own key.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot approve paid speech, switch the approved account, clone a voice or claim distributor acceptance.

steps: 1. Attach a rights-cleared TXT, Markdown or DOCX manuscript to this client order.
2. In the narration desk, select that file and a licensed stock voice.
3. Review the exact source segments. After source changes, prepare them again before approval.
guide.skipped: A filename or cached digest is not evidence. Current stored bytes and current manuscript rights must agree.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar reads the actual bounded file and rechecks the current client and rights. Unreadable or unsupported files refuse.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing outside Chausar while importing the manuscript. Any later AI or speech call asks separately.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot borrow another client source, invent rights or send a private manuscript to the cloud.

steps: 1. Install ffmpeg and whisper.cpp yourself on the desktop computer.
2. Open a current narration segment with its actual audio. Choose Transcribe and measure.
3. Listen and approve the exact audio, master it, then listen again to the newly measured file.
guide.skipped: Missing tools or measurements never pass. Automatic word similarity cannot judge tone or natural pacing.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: The desktop copies current audio bytes to local scratch, transcribes without an expected-text prompt, measures and removes scratch files afterward.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing to a speech-recognition provider. These installed tools run on the desktop.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot install tools, enter made-up measurements or replace owner listening approval.

steps: 1. Master and listen to every current segment, then approve export with AI narration disclosure.
2. Read the target distributor current rules and check the exported audio and disclosure yourself.
3. Upload through your own distributor account. Check its actual acceptance response.
guide.skipped: A technical pass is not acceptance. ACX and unqualified external Google Play synthetic narration remain blocked.

charges.line: No charge.

guide.checks: Chausar checks source, actual audio, owner listening and current rights before export. It does not check a distributor login.
guide.sends: Sends: nothing to a distributor. The owner downloads and submits the approved files manually.
guide.agentLimits: Agents cannot upload, submit, accept terms or promise distributor acceptance.

steps: 1. Create an app password in your own Bluesky account. Record the exact handle and public server.
2. In Connections, open More ways to connect, then Open networks. Enter the exact account and credential and approve its connection check.
3. Review and accept the draft. Record the client approval where required, then approve each exact destination on Today.
guide.skipped: Use an app password, not the account password. Plain text only, within three hundred graphemes.

guide.checks: Chausar verifies the account or channel through its official API. The credential stays in memory for this session.

steps: 1. Create a token for your own Mastodon instance with permission to write statuses. Record its exact account.
2. In Connections, open More ways to connect, then Open networks. Enter the exact account and credential and approve its connection check.
3. Review and accept the draft. Record the client approval where required, then approve each exact destination on Today.
